headlines.text: Flash back to 2023, when FTR vs. The Young Bucks fought tooth and nail for the AEW World Tag Team Titles, appearing on All In: London, rated 8.40 ? an excellent showing. This stood as the 60th match in AEW World Tag Team Titles history ? a genuinely rare milestone for that title. FTR fought off an emotional challenge from The Young Bucks in front of the record-breaking Wembley crowd, retaining the AEW World Tag Team Championship.

Rewind to 2025, when Darby Allin vs. Claudio Castagnoli settled things in a Falls Count Anywhere match, closing out the card as the main event on Dynamite, rated 8.47 ? an excellent showing in a hard-fought men's division clash. Allin battled Castagnoli through a shopping cart, a television and multiple tables in a Falls Count Anywhere war, finishing him with a pair of Coffin Drops.

On this day in 2020, Brian Pillman Jr. competed under the AEW banner for the first time against The Butcher and The Blade vs. The Lucha Brothers vs. Garrison & Pillman Jr. vs. Janela & Kiss vs. The Butcher vs. The Blade vs. Penta El Zero M vs. Rey Fenix vs. Griff Garrison vs. Joey Janela vs. Sonny Kiss, appearing on Dynamite, rated 5.12.

secondaries.text: Back on this day in 2021, The Lucha Brothers vs. Jurassic Express met in a Tournament Match, kicking off the show on Rampage, rated 8.12 ? one of the better matches of the year.

2023 brought us this moment: MJF vs. Adam Cole fought tooth and nail for the AEW World Heavyweight Title, appearing on All In: London, rated 8.49 ? a hard-hitting, high-quality battle. In a match that saw both men repeatedly refuse to turn on the other despite Roderick Strong's interference, MJF retained the AEW World Title over Adam Cole with a small package, closing with the two embracing.

That Sunday in 2023, gold changed shoulders as the AEW World Trios Titles found a new champion as Acclaimed & B.Gunn vs. House of Black battled it out in an Open House match, appearing on All In: London, rated 5.62 ? ending the champion's reign at 8 defenses. House of Black showed a rare moment of sportsmanship, handing their own trios titles over to The Acclaimed and Billy Gunn, who celebrated with the biggest scissor party in wrestling history.
